title: DropdownMenu
wrapsNative: Menu, with Button, Toggle, Picker, Section, Divider and a nested Menu as its items; buttonStyle(.monarch()) on the Menu for the trigger
summary: A list of actions that opens from a button is the standard SwiftUI Menu. Monarch ships nothing; the trigger takes the Monarch button style.
whenToUse: For several related actions behind one button, such as Actions or a More button on a row. Put a Toggle in the menu for an item that is on or off, a Picker for one choice out of several, and a Menu for a submenu.
whenNotToUse: Not for choosing a form value on its own (use a Picker with the menu style). For actions on a row or card the person presses and holds, use contextMenu, which takes the same items. For a destructive action that needs confirming, use confirmationDialog.
api: Button(_ title: String, systemImage: String, role: ButtonRole? = nil, action: () -> Void)
Picker(_ title: String, selection: Binding<SelectionValue>, content: () -> Content)
func contextMenu<MenuItems: View>(menuItems: () -> MenuItems) -> some View

states.name: open
states.description: The system draws the menu next to the trigger and dims nothing. A tap outside closes it.

states.name: checked
states.description: A Toggle that is on, and the selected option of a Picker, show a checkmark before the title.

states.name: destructive
states.description: A Button with the destructive role is drawn in the system's red.

states.name: disabled
states.description: An item with disabled(true) is dimmed and cannot be chosen.

appearance: The menu is drawn by the system in every theme and follows light, dark and Increase Contrast. Monarch colours are not applied inside it. The trigger is drawn by MonarchButtonStyle, and the theme's tint colours the checkmarks.
platformNotes: The web builds DropdownMenu from Radix parts (content, item, checkbox item, radio item, label, separator, submenu). On iOS each part is a standard view inside Menu: Button, Toggle, Picker, Section with a header, Divider and a nested Menu. The web item's tone danger is role: .destructive, its icon is systemImage, and its shortcut is keyboardShortcut, which the system shows when a hardware keyboard is attached. Items cannot be given custom layouts or Monarch colours. Android uses the Material 3 DropdownMenu in the same way.
accessibility: System behaviour: the trigger is a button, and the items are read in order with their checked state.
System behaviour: the menu is dismissed with the escape gesture or a tap outside, and focus returns to the trigger.
An icon-only trigger needs a label: use Label("Actions", systemImage:) with labelStyle(.iconOnly) or accessibilityLabel.
The system gives each item a row at least 44 points high.
edgeCases: The system may reverse the order of items when the menu opens upwards; set menuOrder(.fixed) to keep the order.
A menu closes after any item is chosen, including a Toggle; set menuActionDismissBehavior(.disabled) on an item that should keep it open.
primaryAction on Menu makes a tap run an action and a long press open the menu, which is the split-button behaviour.

parityExceptions.reason: The web menu is a styled popover; on iPhone the menu is the system Menu, whose surface, section header, check mark and destructive red are drawn by iOS and cannot take Monarch colours or show a shortcut hint. The trigger label and the items, their order and the checked item match the web.
parityExceptions.convention: HIG: system menus and date pickers keep the system's own look
